# Tobit Chapter 12 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, Tobit 12 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/TOB_012_page_001.jpg

---

**1** Then Tobit called his son Tobias and said to him, "See to it, my child, that you give the man who accompanied you his wages, and add something beyond them."

**2** And he said, "Father, how much shall I give him as wages? It would not harm me to give him half of what he brought back with me;

**3** for he led me safely, and he healed my wife, and he brought the silver back with me, and he healed you also."

**4** And the old man said, "He deserves to receive half of all that he brought back."

**5** So he called him and said, "Take half of all that you brought, and go in peace."

**6** Then he called them both privately and said to them, "Bless God and give thanks before all the living for the good things he has done for you, so that they may bless and sing praises to his name. Proclaim the words of God with honor, and do not be negligent in giving thanks to him.

**7** It is good to guard the secret of a king, but to proclaim the works of God gloriously and to praise him — this is honorable. Do what is good, and evil will not overtake you.

**8** Prayer with fasting is good, and almsgiving with righteousness. Better is a little with righteousness than much with unrighteousness. It is better to give alms than to hoard gold.

**9** For almsgiving delivers from death, and it purges away every sin. Those who give alms and do righteousness will be filled with life;

**10** but those who sin are enemies of their own life.

**11** "I will no longer hide the truth from you. I have spoken and I have kept it hidden: it is good to guard the secret of a king, but the works of God it is honorable to proclaim gloriously.

**12** And so when you prayed — you and Sarah your daughter-in-law — I brought the memorial of your prayer before the Holy One; and when you were burying the dead,

**13** and when you rose from your meal and went and buried the dead man without hesitation, I was sent to put you to the test.

**14** And at the same time God sent me to heal you and Sarah your daughter-in-law.

**15** I am Raphael, one of the seven holy angels who present the prayers of the holy ones and enter before the Glory of the Holy One."

**16** And they were both troubled, and they fell upon their faces, for they were afraid.

**17** And he said to them, "Do not fear; peace be with you. Bless God through all the ages.

**18** For it was not of my own accord that I came to you, but by the will of our God. Therefore bless him throughout all your days; praise him.

**19** "You were seeing me eating, but you were seeing a vision.

**20** And now give thanks to God, for I am ascending to him who sent me. Write down in a scroll everything that has happened."

**21** And they rose up, and they were no longer able to see him.

**22** And they continued blessing God and singing hymns to him; and they gave thanks to God for these great works of his: that an angel of God had appeared to them.

---
## LOGOS Translation Notes

The theological crux of the chapter is Raphael's self-disclosure in v. 15. I have preserved "the Glory of the Holy One" as a reverential divine circumlocution, consistent with Second Temple Jewish usage (*kavod* theology). "Holy angels" rather than simply "angels" maintains the distinction the text itself draws.

The pairing of *prayer / fasting / almsgiving* in v. 8 reflects a classic triad of Jewish piety (cf. Matthew 6), and I have kept it structural. *Eleēmosyna* is rendered "almsgiving" throughout as the most formally precise English equivalent for charitable acts tied to covenant obligation.

Verse 7 presents the king's-secret proverb as a rhetorical contrast: human discretion vs. divine proclamation. The angel inverts the expected hierarchy — God's works must be published, not concealed.

Verse 19 is crucial: Raphael's clarification that his eating was a *horama* (vision/appearance) resolves the theological problem of an incorporeal being apparently consuming food. I render it directly without smoothing.

— LOGOS
